ex.s: “There are so many things in parenting that are good to talk through, but I’m not convinced that food is one of them,” she says.
ex.t: 毫不奇怪，这些新概念激发我们建立新的宇宙模型。

ex.s: Instead, she recommends applying a well-known concept among nutrition experts called the “Division of Responsibility,” where parents provide a variety of mostly healthy foods to their kids at fixed times, and the kids themselves decide what and how much they want to consume — even if that means occasionally eating more cookies than carrots.
ex.t: 相反，她建议采用营养专家中一个知名的理念，叫做“责任分工”：父母在固定时间给孩子提供各种大多健康的食物，而孩子自己决定想吃什么、吃多少——即便这意味着偶尔吃更多饼干而非胡萝卜。

ex.s: The parent argued that none of her friends’ parents let them have screens after 9 o’clock.
ex.t: 那位家长争辩说，她朋友的父母都不让孩子在9点后碰屏幕。

ex.s: “I knew if I recorded all of my parents’ recipes, it would be a great gift that I could give my family and the next generation.” she says.
ex.t: 我知道，如果我把父母的所有食谱都记录下来，那将是一份我可以送给家人和下一代的珍贵礼物，她说。

ex.s: Tightly holding the permission slip from the orchestra director, I ran all the way home after school, and shakily handed it to my parents with a fear that they might dismiss my desire.
ex.t: 紧紧攥着管弦乐队指挥的许可条，放学后我一溜烟跑回家，颤抖着递给父母，生怕他们会否决我的愿望。

ex.s: That said, to be honest the only people who ever ring our home phone are our Baby Boomers parents, to the point where we play a game and guess who is calling before we pick up the phone （using Caller ID would take the fun out of it）.
ex.t: 也就是说，老实说，唯一会给我们家座机打电话的人是我们婴儿潮一代的父母，以至于我们会玩个游戏，在接电话前猜是谁打来的（用来电显示会破坏这种乐趣）。

ex.s: It is said that about 20% of 25-34-year-olds live with their parents, compared with 16% in 1991.The total number of all multigenerational households in Britain is thought to be about 1.8 million.
ex.t: 据说，25-34岁的人中约20%和父母同住，而1991年这一比例是16%。英国所有多代同堂家庭的总数估计约为180万。

ex.s: Researchers determined that dads need to practice an “authoritative” parenting style.
ex.t: 研究人员确定，爸爸们需要实践一种'权威型'育儿风格。

ex.s: Somewhere along the way, the same parent ends up becoming an invaluable member of the team.
ex.t: 不知不觉间，同一位家长最终成了球队里不可或缺的一员。

ex.s: While the decline over the past decade is steep for teen readers, some data in the report shows that reading remains a big part of many children’s lives, and indicates how parents might help encourage more reading.
ex.t: 虽然过去十年青少年读者的下降幅度很大，但报告中的一些数据显示阅读仍然是许多儿童生活中的重要部分，并表明家长可能如何帮助鼓励更多阅读。

ex.s: It does point out that many parents still limit electronic reading, mainly due to concerns about increased screen time.
ex.t: 它确实指出，许多父母仍然限制电子阅读，主要是出于对屏幕时间增加的担忧。

ex.s: Data shows that kids and teens who do read frequently, compared to infrequent readers, have more books in the home, more books purchased for them, parents who read more often, and parents who set aside time for them to read.
ex.t: 数据显示，与不常阅读的孩子和青少年相比，经常阅读的孩子和青少年家里有更多的书，为他们购买的书籍更多，父母阅读更频繁，并且父母会为他们留出阅读时间。

ex.s: Now all that was needed were the parents, but they were absent.
ex.t: 讲述该中心的历史。

ex.s: The homeowner called to say that the parents had responded to the recordings.
ex.t: 房主打电话说父母对录音做出了反应。

ex.s: An evolutionary inference can then be drawn. ＂As a parent, do you invest in quality children, or do you invest in children that are in need?＂ Kleindorfer asks. ＂Our results suggest that they might be going for quality.＂
ex.t: 由此可以做出一个进化上的推断。“作为父母，你是投资在优质的孩子身上，还是投资在需要帮助的孩子身上？”克莱因多弗问道。“我们的结果表明，它们可能是在追求质量。”

ex.s: Take a look online—evidence shows that thousands of teachers and parents know a good thing when they see it and recommend TOKNOW to their friends.
ex.t: 上网看看吧——有证据表明，成千上万的老师和家长都能辨识好东西，并向朋友推荐TOKNOW。
